O.outcome_detail: Presence of nutrition-counselling competencies in the curriculum

cells.quote: Overall, almost all counselling competencies required for primary preventive NC are covered by NKLM 2.0. Content on nudging or sensitive communication about body weight could not be found.
cells.note: This is a qualitative curriculum content analysis, not an intervention comparison or learner-outcome study; the treatment/comparison fields represent curriculum content that was present versus absent.

cells.note: This is a qualitative curriculum-content comparison, not a learning intervention; the positive direction denotes that NKLM 2.0 covered almost all required competencies, with the quoted gaps.

D.comparison: curriculum specification including teaching formats and time frames

O.outcome_detail: specification of teaching formats and time requirements

cells.quote: NKLM 2.0 did not specify time frames, but rather recommendations for the semester or academic year and the level of competence to be achieved regarding learning objectives. Teaching formats were not included, and recommendations were rarely mentioned, for example, “Can be implemented very well in communication courses”.
cells.note: The entry paraphrases this as neither teaching formats nor time frames being specified, while the study notes semester or academic-year recommendations.

cells.quote: In conclusion, all communication competencies were demonstrated multiple times in NKLM 2.0.

O.outcome_detail: coverage of competencies required for preventive nutritional counselling

result.effect: 1,426 coded segments; 5 codes had no teaching content

cells.quote: NKLM 2.0 covers most of the competencies required for adequate preventive medical NC. There are gaps in nutritional knowledge (nutrition of breastfeeding mothers, cooking and kitchen techniques, eating behaviour) and in nutrition counselling competencies (nudging, sensitive communication about body weight, systemic counselling).
cells.note: This was a qualitative curriculum-content analysis, not an intervention or learner-outcome comparison.
